label: sparse conjunction: sequences with t/c after an l/x/h/3/v-type token (no clean rule)
explanation: Very sparse (0.036% of steps) and weak (max 0.205, nearly flat magnitudes). Never fires at t<3; spread across late original steps, the delimiter, and early copy steps, with a peak at the first copy-input step (recall_idx==1, 32% of mass). Activity is enriched in sequences that start with l/x/3/h/v and contain t and c early on (prev2_tok t 7x, next_out c 8.6x, in_tok l 8.3x), but no single variable has an active rate above 0.3%, so every predicate tried has precision under 3%. The best one (copy step 1, first token in {l,x,3,h,v}, second token in a v/c/x/l/3/t/w/q set) gets dev F1 0.05 and mass recall 0.28. It does not fire on early original steps (t<3), and it rarely fires late in the copy phase (recall_idx>=4). The feature looks like a high-order conjunction of specific token identities that the provided variables cannot capture.
